items.objective_statement: apply the formula for density: ρ = m / V
items.stem: A uniform solid is divided into two equal pieces. Each piece has

misconception.label: Halving the mass alone would halve the density, but the volume halves too.
Neither the mass nor the volume falls to a quarter.
Nothing about cutting a block makes it denser.

steps: Density is ρ = m / V.
Cutting the block in half halves the mass and halves the volume.
Halving the top and the bottom of a fraction leaves it unchanged, so each half has the same density as the whole. Density is a property of the substance, not of how much of it there is.
solution.answer_line: the same density

items.objective_statement: draw a line of ‘best fit’ for a set of plotted values
items.stem: When experimental readings are plotted, a best-fit line is used because it

misconception.label: Being easier to draw is not a reason for preferring it.
Only a relationship of direct proportion passes through the origin.

options.text: is always steeper than the joined line

misconception.label: The gradient of the best fit line is whatever the readings give; it is not systematically steeper.

options.text: averages out the uncertainty in the individual readings

steps: Every reading carries a small error, so no single point is exactly right.
Joining the points repeats those errors in the shape of the line.
A single line drawn with the points balanced above and below it averages the errors out, so its gradient is the best estimate available.
solution.answer_line: averages out the uncertainty in the individual readings
